searchText: This does seem like a possible attack, especially if the colluding includer selects transactions that are expensive to simulate (e.g. requiring lots of account storage access). The non-colluding builders would be forced to re-simulate the inclusion list txs to see if they are includable in every block they build, adding latency to their block submission. The colluding builder avoids this latency and therefore builds and submits faster giving it a speed advantage in auctions. Relays could avoid this issue in their auctions by doing the inclusion themselves (it is similar to multi-party block construction already implemented by some relay operators: https://docs.blockspace.forum/mpbc/live-metrics/#overview) - but that does not solve the issue in the general case.
